P1.evidence: This is the one call in the batch with a pre-qualifying setter, so P1a applies — and the rep never read back Kim's notes or the application. Kim surfaced only because the prospect raised him twice, unprompted, including the fact that he had been sent a preparation video he had not watched. The frame ran in the usual compressed three-part form. Time availability was confirmed ('you have the 4.45 to an hour available?'), which earns a partial on P1c, but no frame agreement was sought. Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Work was covered properly and at length — 'so you're not working currently at the moment?' opened a genuinely useful exploration of the non-compete, the return-to-work window and the pressure of transformation roles. Everything else in the baseline arrived by the prospect's own initiative. Age, height and weight are all on record but volunteered rather than systematically taken. Health conditions were never asked: the Function Health biomarker panel, the LDL and HDL trend and the systemic inflammation were all offered unprompted. Injuries were never asked, and the knee pain — the single physical constraint on the call, and the reason he stopped his current training — was volunteered twice and never once probed by the rep. Diet was never asked despite the prospect twice starting to describe it. Sleep and energy were not touched at all, on a 58-year-old.

P3.evidence: The first half was excellent. 'With where your health is right now... would you say that you're happy with it, if you were to be completely honest with yourself and me?' produced an immediate no, and the follow-up produced the best line of the call: 'you're not at peace with yourself.' The rep caught it and reflected it — 'You said a very strong sentence... Tell me more' — which is exactly right. The success question ran twice, once for appearance and once for feeling. Then it stopped. P3f was asked ('What other arenas would you say have been affected?'), the prospect deflected with 'I don't know if anything, I mean, it's just mostly mental', and the rep accepted the deflection rather than working it. P3g never happened at all, and this is the significant failure of the call: the prospect opened at 00:01:01 with 'I lost one of my parents in November and I realized... I've got three kids and I want to be around for them', and again at 00:06:27 with 'my mom was 89. So if I can get to 89, I want to be walking it, not in a wheelchair.' Legacy, mortality and fatherhood were handed over in the first six minutes and never returned to. The reflect-back came as a paraphrase rather than the scripted contrast.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase 4 in the batch. The framing move ran well — 'a mentor once told me, what has kept you stuck in the past will find a way to keep you stuck in the future' — followed by 'if you were to be super critical as to why you aren't in the body that you want to be... what really has been the main thing for you?', which produced a long, honest answer about growing up in India, building himself intellectually, and never prioritising the physical. P4f ran almost verbatim in its intended form: 'what is the rationale for you getting outside help as opposed to ChatGPT and you to tick this? Information is so abundant.' And the prospect named the gap himself with unusual clarity: 'I would say I'm diligent, Farooq. I just get lazy. If I'm on my own... if I can sneak away, have that extra carb for the day, I might do it.' Past attempts were the weaker part — the trainer in his 40s was mentioned but never unpacked for what specifically ended it.

P5.evidence: Not merely skipped but consciously declined. At 00:20:30 the rep said: 'And there's no point in me going into the doom and gloom. I'm pretty sure you're aware of what things look like if, God forbid, you continue on a trajectory like that.' That is the rep opting out of the highest-weighted phase in the process on the assumption the prospect has already done it for himself. P5d gets a partial for the want-or-need question and 'why are you having this conversation today as opposed to in February?', both of which are urgency probes rather than cost-of-inaction framing. Fourth consecutive call in this batch with no consequence frame, and here uniquely the rep articulated the decision to skip it out loud.

P6.evidence: P6a ran cleanly and late: 'The most important question of the day is, do you feel internally capable of having success?' produced a strong answer about arriving as an immigrant with two suitcases. But the all-in question was never asked. And P6c failed in the same way as the Roy Norman call: the alignment check was run after the pillars, the answer was an explicit five or six out of ten with a stated reason — 'I got to try to know whether it's going to make sense... It's not a 10 because I haven't tried it. I don't know what it's going to do for me and whether I can even keep up' — and the rep proceeded straight to the price. The script says return to phase 5 on hesitation. Phase 5 had been deliberately skipped, so there was nothing to return to, and thirty seconds later the prospect was pricing a local personal trainer against the offer.

P11.evidence: No close was achieved, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable. A follow-up call was scheduled for Monday the 11th, which is appropriate given the prospect's stated evaluation process.

objection_plays.detail: A clear think-about-it: 'I will give it some thought tonight' and 'I don't do anything impulsive.' Two moves ran and ran well. The rep asked what was still outstanding — 'What else would you say that you need to think about before making, feeling confident enough to make a decision?' — which is the play's diagnostic move and produced the real answer (not money, but whether he will get what he needs and how it compares to a local option). And he made a version of 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is' fitted to a consultant: 'a criteria of putting pen to paper, really thinking about things, it's like a sensible thing to do. But the best data point you can give yourself, honestly, is actually lived experience.' That is well judged for this prospect. The rest did not run — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no 'that man you want to be, how does he decide right now', and no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'.

Doubt was live and specific: 'can I keep up? Can I do this?' and 'I don't know what it's going to do for me.' The rep's response was structural rather than scripted — reduce the commitment via the upgrade credit, then offer the trial — which is essentially the BRIDGE move ('I'm not asking you to see the whole other side, just take the first step') delivered as a product rather than as language. The certainty question, the pleasure-versus-pain question, the PLANE and BURNED BEFORE moves were all absent.

Money was explicitly not the objection — 'Financially, I don't need to think' and 'committing to something is not the issue. Funding is fine.' Correctly, the rep did not run the play. The price-related resistance here is value comparison, scored below.

Timing favoured the sale and both parties knew it — a three-to-six-month window before he returns to an intense role. The rep even framed it: 'right now you have a three to six month window where you have time to pour into yourself.'

The known cheaper-alternative gap, but in a harder variant that should be logged separately: the substitute is not cheaper, it is comparable in price and superior in one dimension. He can price an in-person trainer at his golf club four to five times a week and believes it comes in under $4,000, with hands-on correction the remote model cannot match. The rep's only move was the LeBron James analogy, and the prospect took it apart in one sentence: 'it depends on where you're starting, right? If you can't get the ball in, LeBron's not going to be able to help you virtually.' That is the correct rebuttal and there was no answer to it. The genuine differentiators — portability across constant international travel, and the fact that a local trainer is useless when he is in a hotel in Asia — were named by the prospect himself and never picked up by the rep.

Scope overlap with an existing clinical team, the same gap seen on the Roy Norman call the previous day. This prospect has primary care at Mayo Clinic and a Mayo nutritionist already engaged specifically on this issue: 'there are elements of this I'm going to get here anyway, because of the system I'm in.' Pillar two therefore duplicates a service he already receives from a clinical provider, and there is no reduced-scope option and no scripted way to position the pillars as complementary. Two independent prospects raised this in two days.

notes: Phase 4 was genuinely strong and 'you're not at peace with yourself' was well caught. The call was lost — or at least deferred — on three specific things. The rep declined to run phase 5 out loud. He never went near the mother's death or the three children despite both being offered in the opening minute. And he took a five-or-six-out-of-ten alignment score straight to the price. The result is that the only true-ICP prospect in this batch walked away to price a local trainer, and the rep's counter to a comparable in-person alternative was an analogy that did not survive contact. Coach the return to phase 5 on hesitation, and build a real answer to 'why remote when in-person costs the same' — portability was sitting there unused.
